title: Enhancement of liquid-liquid phase transition under shear flow
abstract: In a liquid--liquid transition (LLT), a single-component liquid transforms into another liquid with different density and viscosity. Flow therefore couples to the transition, but the effect of shear flow is not understood. Here we investigate the LLT under shear with a two-order-parameter hydrodynamic model in which the viscosity depends on the non-conserved structural order parameter. Under shear, a fluctuation of the order parameter drives a compressional flow through the viscosity, and the resulting density change enhances the order parameter fluctuation. In a linear analysis, this feedback destabilizes the metastable liquid above a critical shear rate $\dotγ_{\rm c}$ for wavevectors in particular directions. Because the flow rotates the wavevector, a fluctuation grows only for a finite time duration, and its amplification is determined by the dimensionless shear rate $\dotγ/\dotγ_{\rm c}$ and the second dimensionless number $Λ$, the ratio of the thermodynamic relaxation rate of the order parameter to $\dotγ_{\rm c}$. In hydrodynamic simulations, shear above about $\dotγ_{\rm c}$ induces the transition in the metastable region when $Λ\gtrsim1$. The transition proceeds by nucleation of domains whose morphology becomes anisotropic. The incubation time decreases and the onset of the viscosity increase is accelerated as $\dotγ$ and $Λ$ increase. These results imply that the shear rate is a control variable of LLT in addition to temperature and pressure, selecting whether and how a metastable liquid transforms.
summary: This work theoretically and numerically investigates how shear flow drives a liquid-liquid phase transition (LLT) in a liquid. It shows that shear acts as a new control parameter, destabilizing the metastable liquid above a critical shear rate ($\dot{\gamma}_c$). The transition is characterized by anisotropic domain nucleation, demonstrating that external flow profoundly alters the thermodynamics of phase change.
main_problem: The paper investigates how shear flow influences the liquid-liquid phase transition (LLT) in a single-component liquid.
main_result: Shear rate acts as a control variable for the LLT, inducing the transition above a critical shear rate ($\dot{\gamma}_c$) via a feedback mechanism that enhances order parameter fluctuations.
method: The study employs a two-order-parameter hydrodynamic model, analyzing stability using linear theory and confirming results with full hydrodynamic simulations.
model_or_system: The system is a single-component liquid undergoing LLT, modeled using a two-order-parameter hydrodynamic framework where viscosity depends on the structural order parameter. Governing equations include mass and momentum conservation, alongside the evolution equation for the non-conserved order parameter.
key_observables: The structure factor $S_\varphi(q)$, the critical shear rate $\dot{\gamma}_c$, and the amplification factor $G$ of fluctuations.
important_parameters: Dimensionless shear rate ($\dot{\gamma}/\dot{\gamma}_c$) and the ratio $\Lambda$ of the thermodynamic relaxation rate to $\dot{\gamma}_c$.
main_assumptions: The analysis uses an isothermal limit and assumes the kinetic coefficient $L$ is small, simplifying the dynamics to non-conserved kinetics.
figures_summary: The notes detail the mathematical framework for analyzing fluctuation growth and structure factor evolution under shear, but do not describe specific figure contents.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the hydrodynamic model and governing equations, proceeding through linear stability analysis in Fourier space, and concluding with nonlinear hydrodynamic simulations to confirm the shear-induced transition.
why_interesting: The coupling between external fields (shear flow) and intrinsic phase transition dynamics is a key non-equilibrium problem relevant to understanding complex fluid behavior, which shares mathematical parallels with driven quantum systems.
